newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA SET FOR SRI LANKAN BATTING RECORD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA SET FOR SRI LANKAN BATTING RECORD.

text.p: Opener Sanath Jayasuriya was on course to becoming the highest scorer in Sri Lankan cricket on Tuesday.
He had plundereed 230 not out off India by lunch on the fourth day of the first test and was within sight of Aravinda de Silva's record 267 against New Zealand in Wellington on the 1990-91 tour.
Jayasuriya's second wicket partner Roshan Mahanama was also enjoying himself on the lifeless pitch and had made an unbeaten 150.
By lunch the pair had put on 379 together and lifted Sri Lanka to 418 for one in reply to 537 for eight declared. With two sessions and one day left a draw looked inevitable.

Jayasuriya became only the third Sri Lankan batsmen to score a test double century when he flicked Venkatesh Prasad off his legs for four in the seventh over of the morning. He hit 25 fours in a stay of 452 minutes facing 327 balls.
Mahanama reached 150 for the third time in his career shortly before lunch. He had batted 496 minutes, faced 346 balls and hit 19 fours.
